before.title: Artemis platform launches commercially
before.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support. Introduces Artemis training. At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance. The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts. Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required.

outcomes.description: Launch campaign and dated follow-up activities are specified in ncc_1980_campaign.json and NCC_1980_CAMPAIGN.md. Compatibility through 2000 is a commitment with eligibility and maintenance obligations, not evidence of future fulfilment.

after.title: Artemis platform launches commercially
after.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support. Introduces Artemis training. At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance. The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts. Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required. Logix introduced an Artemis 128 KiB office configuration with two floppy drives, a Color Monitor II, keyboard, AIONix, Business Tools and one year of support. A second configuration added a 5 MB disk subsystem. Customers could add Abacus 3 from November 1980 and networking from May 1981.
